text:
sara-sales: Quick question — customer wants Private deployment (on-prem tunnel + VPC) for LLM POC. They insist on preserving client source IP to their downstream services. Options they've proposed: VPC peering + NAT, PrivateLink interface endpoint, or an egress proxy in their datacenter. Any recommendations on simplest route that preserves src IP and fits our on-prem connector?

mike-netops: @sara-sales if they need original client IP seen by on-prem, PrivateLink (interface endpoints) will show our connector's ENI IPs, so not preserved. VPC peering can preserve src if you don't NAT. But if traffic traverses a NAT gateway it's changed.

lee-se: For Private deployment we usually offer two patterns: 1) direct VPC peering + transit routing, 2) interface endpoint (PrivateLink) with a proxy in their VPC that forwards. Peering is simpler but cross-account VPC routes and security approvals required.

devon-arch: Also consider security/compliance: peering opens full L3 routes; PrivateLink is more controlled (service-specific) and often easier for security teams. If they require src IP for auth, best to use peering and avoid NAT on the path, or have X-Forwarded-For at the proxy layer.

sara-sales: They also asked about firewall rules / ports and cost impact. Any short checklist I can give them?

mike-netops: Minimal allowlist for privatedeploy connector: outbound TCP 443 to our control plane, and TCP 443 to model endpoints (if egress). If peering, allow BGP/route propagation? Provide sample:

```
# sample SG / firewall
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 10.10.0.0/16 port 443
allow tcp from our connector IPs to 203.0.113.0/24 port 443
```

Also note PrivateLink adds per-GB/data processing charges on some clouds + interface endpoint hourly costs.

devon-arch: Pricing note for customer: PrivateLink = interface endpoints (hourly + data), peering = no interface endpoint charges but you may pay cross-AZ data transfer. For sustained heavy tokens, peering + direct routing typically cheaper.

lee-se: For the POC, if they can't get peering approved fast, propose a short-term solution: deploy a lightweight egress proxy bridge in their VPC (NGINX) that forwards real client IP in X-Forwarded-For and accepts TLS from our connector. That preserves client IP at application layer (not TCP). Works for most apps.

sara-sales: Any security questionnaire phrasing I can copy re: telemetry/audit? They want "where does logs/metadata flow".

devon-arch: Add: "Control plane metadata (job scheduling, health checks) flows to our hosted control plane endpoints in us-east-1 over TLS. Request payloads may be routed via customer network for Private deploy; we do not persist customer plaintext data outside their VPC."

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: connectors/agent v2.1 required for srcip-preserve-workaround. See doc: https://redwood.example/internal/privatedeploy/net-ops

mike-netops: I'll start a short runbook and DM infra team. Can someone ping customer for their VPC CIDR and security contact?

sara-sales: @mike-netops will ping. Thanks all :thumbsup:
